decision_conditions: The proposed development, by virtue of its insufficient details on materiality and design, the oversized dormers and a significant loss of vegetated garden would appear visually intrusive, incongruous, overly dominant and out of keeping with the character and appearance of the host building and the surrounding area of which it forms part. The proposal is therefore contrary to Section 12 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policies D4, D5 of the London Plan (2021), CP30 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), DMD6, DMD11, DMD13 and DMD37 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014), Policy HW-1, HW-12, HW-13, HW-14 of Hadley Wood Neighbourhood Plan (2023).

The proposed development, by virtue of the fenestration locations and inadequate boundary treatment would cause poor outlook and privacy concern to ground floor unit and result in substandard and inappropriate accommodation incapable of meeting the reasonable needs of occupiers contrary to Section 12 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), to Policies D3 and D6 of the London Plan (2021), to Policies CP4 and CP30 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), to Policies DMD6, DMD7, DMD8 and DMD37 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014), and the Housing Design Standards London Plan Guidance (2023).

The proposed development, by virtue of its proximity to the boundary and inadequate separation distances, would result in unacceptable overlooking and loss of privacy to neighbouring properties, particularly 1A Corbar Close. Furthermore, the proposed padel court, would introduce unacceptable noise and disturbance to adjacent occupiers, contrary to Section 12 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policies D3 and D6 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CP30 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD6, DMD8 and DMD10 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014), Policy HW-1, HW-12 and HW-13, and HW-14 Hadley Wood Neighbourhood Plan (2023).

The proposed development, by virtue of the excessive pull distance and narrow access and insufficient turning ahead for refuse collection vehicles, fails to provide refuse storage and collection arrangements that meet operational requirements. The proposal would result in significant operational difficulties for waste collection and inconvenience for residents, leading to poor service delivery and potential highway obstruction. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy T7 of the London Plan (2021), Policies CP24, CP25 and CP26 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), and Policies DMD45, DMD47 and DMD48 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The proposed development fails to demonstrate that existing trees will be adequately retained and protected. The proposal provides insufficient justification for the removal of 18 trees. The submitted arboricultural documents do not assess the full impact of all aspects of the development—including the basement, padel court, changes to ground levels, hard surfacing, drainage, and boundary structures—on retained tree, contrary to Section 15 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policies G6 and G7 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CP34 and 36 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD79 and DMD80 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014), Policy HW-7 Hadley Wood Neighbourhood Plan (2023).

The proposed development fails to provide any mechanism to secure the statutory Biodiversity Net Gain or demonstrate the required 10% uplift in biodiversity value, contrary to Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as inserted by the Environment Act 2021), Section 16 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy G6 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CP36 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD78 and DMD79 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014), and Policy HW-7 of the Hadley Wood Neighbourhood Plan (2023)

The proposed development fails to demonstrate that adequate groundwater flood mitigation measures have been incorporated into the design, which would increase groundwater flooding risk on-site or in the surrounding area, contrary to guidance in Section 14 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024); Policies SI 12 and SI 13 of the London Plan (2021); Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy (2010) and Policies DMD59, DMD60 and DMD61 of the Development Management Document (2014).

The proposed development, by virtue of the lack of lighting arrangement along access routes, would result in poorly lit spaces that prejudice highway safety and are vulnerable to anti-social behaviour and crime, contrary to Section 12 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), to Policies D11 and T4 of the London Plan (2021), to Policies CP4 and CP30 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), and to Policies DMD7, DMD8 and DMD37 and DMD 47 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).
